objective.text: Use an explicit allowed origin for credentialed cross-origin requests rather than a wildcard response.

difficulty.rationale: Return a credential-compatible origin policy without granting arbitrary origins access.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: The allowed frontend is https://app.example.test. Its browser request includes eligible cookies, and the endpoint is meant to allow this origin.

stem: The response has Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, and the browser refuses access. Which response policy fixes this mismatch?

options.text: Keep the wildcard and add Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Cookie.
options.rationale: Allowing a request-header name does not change the credentialed origin rule.
options.misconception: Allowing a request-header name does not change the credentialed origin rule.

options.text: Echo any Origin value without validating it against an allowlist.
options.rationale: That removes the intended origin restriction and can expose credentialed responses to untrusted origins.
options.misconception: That removes the intended origin restriction and can expose credentialed responses to untrusted origins.

options.text: Keep the wildcard and repeat Access-Control-Allow-Credentials twice.
options.rationale: Repeating the credential header does not make the wildcard compatible.
options.misconception: Repeating the credential header does not make the wildcard compatible.

options.text: Return the allowed frontend origin explicitly and allow credentials.
options.rationale: Credentialed CORS cannot use a wildcard Allow-Origin response; the server should select an origin from its allowlist.

explanation.summary: Credentialed CORS cannot use a wildcard Allow-Origin response; the server should select an origin from its allowlist.
